limitation.text: Improving code generation typically relies on costly external resources like superior teachers or reliable test oracles, and preference-based fine-tuning can be adversely affected by noisy self-generated supervision.

summary.text: The combination merges direct preference optimization, code generation, and instruction following to enable self-improving code generation without relying on external test oracles or superior teachers. It utilizes behavioral consensus to weight preference pairs, mitigating the impact of noisy self-generated supervision during fine-tuning.

target_user.text: The target user is unverified as the evidence bundle contains no patent assignee categories, repositories, or packages that specify end-user demographics.

jtbd.text: When developers need to improve language model code generation and instruction adherence, they want to fine-tune models using consensus-driven preference optimization so that they can avoid costly external test oracles and noisy self-generated supervision.

value_prop.text: This approach enables code language models to self-improve on instruction-following and code generation tasks without requiring access to superior teacher models or external test oracles.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is axis V (viability), which was designated due to missing evidence in the bundle. We assume that organizations will pay for a consensus-driven direct preference optimization service for code generation.

mvp.text: Run customer interviews and a price acceptance test with engineering teams to validate willingness to pay for a consensus-driven code alignment tool.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 40 percent positive willingness-to-pay responses during price acceptance interviews, motivated by dvf:17.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of interviewed engineering leads express willingness to pay for the proposed code alignment pipeline, as motivated by dvf:17.

open_source.use: Used as an evaluation tool for testing reward models and alignment performance.
Used to evaluate functional requirements and code generation performance.

to_build.text: Build a consensus-driven direct preference optimization module that weights preference pairs by behavioral consensus, as described in paper:2603.29292.
